extracted.intended_audience: governments, executing/implementing agencies, private sector partners, donors, project developers, and other stakeholders seeking ADB financing
extracted.subtask_description: A high-level institutional summary of ADB-administered funds, financing instruments, target recipients, delivery modes, and recent innovations in funding—intended to guide potential partners and borrowers about which funds or instruments apply and on what terms. Covers Ordinary Capital Resources, the Asian Development Fund, special/trust funds, and partnership facilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of financing available
rubrics_metrics.description: ADB offers loans, grants, and technical assistance from Special Funds, Trust Funds, and other sources to help reduce poverty in Asia’s poorest countries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These financing instruments are administered via multiple fund vehicles (special funds, trust funds, partnership facilities) and are meant to support poverty reduction and development objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ordinary Capital Resources (OCR) terms and target recipients
rubrics_metrics.description: Most of ADB's lending comes from its ordinary capital resources (OCR), offered at near-market terms to lower- to middle-income countries—and beginning in 2017—at very low interest rates to lower income countries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR operations are diverse and cover focus areas and sectors supporting ADB's operational priorities; concessional terms may apply for lower-income countries per policy changes since 2017.

rubrics_metrics.name: Asian Development Fund (ADF) purpose and modality
rubrics_metrics.description: ADF provides grants to ADB's lower-income developing member countries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Activities supported by the ADF promote poverty reduction and improvements in the quality of life in the poorer countries of the Asia and Pacific region. ADF functions as a grant-only donor fund for eligible countries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delivery modalities for financing
rubrics_metrics.description: ADB supports projects delivered through both public and private sector operations, advisory services, and knowledge support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Project financing, advisory, and knowledge services are all legitimate channels for delivering development impact; choice of modality should align with project objectives and partner capacity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fund classification (special funds, trust funds, partnership facilities)
rubrics_metrics.description: Browse by: Special Funds | Trust Funds | Partnership Facilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ADB establishes and utilizes different fund vehicles to administer projects; the classification affects governance, eligible activities, and partnership arrangements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partnership administration and stewardship
rubrics_metrics.description: All Funds: ADB also establishes and utilizes other funds and financing facilities to administer for its projects. These may involve partnerships with private entities and/or member countries and are given the same amount of care as ADB's own resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Funds administered with partners are expected to adhere to ADB stewardship standards and oversight practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Private sector investment focus
rubrics_metrics.description: ADB also partners with the private sector by investing in smaller, riskier projects that are innovative, complex, and in challenging markets and sectors through financing programs such as the Trade and Supply Chain Finance Program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Private sector programs target innovation and riskier opportunities that may not attract commercial financing; programmatic vehicles (e.g., Trade and Supply Chain Finance Program) are examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovations and enhancements in funding design
rubrics_metrics.description: An innovation to combine ADF’s equity and lending operations with OCR balance sheet to enhance ADB’s lending capacity, while retaining ADF as a grant-only donor fund to provide grant assistance to eligible countries, took effect on 1 January 2017.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such structural funding innovations are designed to increase overall lending capacity while preserving concessional grant channels for the poorest countries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuation of concessional lending from expanded OCR
rubrics_metrics.description: Concessional lending to poor countries continue from the expanded OCR, on the same terms and conditions as current ADF loans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy ensures that expansion of OCR does not reduce concessional support for poor countries; expanded OCR can carry the same concessional terms previously provided by ADF.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intended project outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: ADB supports projects in developing member countries that create economic and development impact, delivered through both public and private sector operations, advisory services, and knowledge support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Project proposals and financing should be designed to deliver measurable economic and development impact aligned with ADB's strategic priorities (e.g., sustainable, inclusive, resilient growth).

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility by country income level
rubrics_metrics.description: Different funds and terms target countries by income: OCR targets lower- to middle-income countries (with concessional rates for lower income), while ADF targets lower-income/poorest borrowing countries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants and governments should determine appropriate financing vehicles based on country income status and eligibility for grants versus loans.
